Rectangle - Rectangle is a window manager heavily based on Spectacle, written in Swift.

summary.one_liner: Rectangle is a macOS window management app, based on Spectacle and written in Swift, that snaps and resizes windows with keyboard shortcuts and drag-to-edge gestures.
summary.what_it_does: Rectangle moves and resizes the focused window using keyboard shortcuts, menu items, or dragging a window to screen edges and corners (halves, quarters, thirds, fourths, sixths, ninths, eighths, maximize, and almost-maximize). It can tile ordinary windows in rows or columns on the current Space and cycle through distinct grid layouts on repeated presses. Stacked windows can be brought forward one at a time with dedicated cycle actions. Mouse side buttons can be assigned as shortcuts, and individual apps can be ignored so their own shortcuts are not overridden. Actions can also be triggered from the command line or other tools through rectangle:// URLs. Settings can be imported and exported as JSON.
use_cases: snap windows to halves or quarters on macOS
tile multiple windows in rows or columns
keyboard shortcuts to resize and move windows
script window actions via URL or shell
back up and transfer window manager settings
how_to_run: Or download the latest dmg from the Releases page
notable: Snap-by-drag to screen edges, corners, thirds, and fourths, modeled on Spectacle
Tile in Rows and Tile in Columns with balanced grid cycling and configurable limits
Mouse side buttons can be assigned as window action shortcuts
Ignore-app option unregisters shortcuts while a given app is frontmost
Execute actions via rectangle:// URLs and execute-task ignore/unignore commands
caveats: Requires macOS 14+; older macOS versions need v1.100 (10.15–13) or v0.73 (10.13–10.14)
Window animation is marked experimental and may cause issues in edge cases
Cannot move windows between Spaces or desktops, since Apple provides no public API for it
Some apps enforce minimum window sizes that Rectangle cannot override, causing overlap in small layouts
